summary: Accepted after fresh end-to-end review of all 28 current Tape EC cases and referenced runners at source digest sha256:3d1ee7bdcbf4635e73760a26d2b8b126d19ac5aa92e1a1bbb37631b4eaad7ef4. Behavior, efficiency, security, and stability cases bind the current Tape capability claims to concrete CLI, library, HTTP/h2c, generated-client, Raft, bootstrap, operator, soak, auth/admission, guard, meter, NATS JetStream, and Kafka journeys. Assertions pin route sets, error and authorization behavior, event/payload sizes, latency limits, replay ratios, recovery outcomes, and resource plateaus. Oracles are test-owned or externally versioned: generated clients are inspected across TypeScript/Python/Rust, competitor classification comes from a committed official-source fixture, performance thresholds and ratios are computed directly in EC tests, and service-auth independently checks credential-free audit events. Zero-test and prerequisite loopholes are closed: exact filters name live tests; generated clients have one non-ignored integration test; VAT meter-perf uses --include-ignored and selects two ordinary local tests plus the ignored real NATS release test; standalone EC commands use --release --ignored for NATS and Kafka; both real-service runners fail closed when their required service cannot start. Findings empty.
